title: NetherSX2 v2.0 PS2 Emulator on Low-End Android Mali - 4GB RAM Test!
summary: RGB Tech pushes NetherSX2 2.0 on an overclocked Galaxy A30 with Exynos 7904, Mali-G71 MP2 and 4 GB RAM, testing six games across explicit resolution multipliers on a modified Android environment.

blocks.text: The eight-minute test documents its low-end mobile host unusually well: a 14 nm Exynos 7904, two Cortex-A73 and six A53 cores, an overclocked Mali-G71 MP2, 4 GB LPDDR4X, eMMC storage and an S23 FE-derived Android 14 port. After application settings, six unnamed games are shown at 1x through 3x native resolution. Switching multipliers within the same title helps reveal whether a scene is sensitive to graphics load or limited elsewhere.

This is not a stock Galaxy A30. Both CPU/GPU details indicate overclocking, and a custom OS port changes drivers, thermal behavior and stability; those modifications can shorten hardware life or corrupt data. The game names and NetherSX2 package provenance are also absent, while the description links a separate firmware setup video. Do not reproduce voltage or clock changes without device-specific knowledge. Read the recording as an altered-environment experiment, and compare stock clocks, temperatures and legal personal firmware before drawing low-end recommendations.
